heading: How it works
answer: Five phases. Measurement first, because without a baseline nothing later can be proven. Then the fast technical fixes, then on-site content work, then off-site authority building, then monthly measurement that keeps the whole thing honest.

phases.name: Baseline
phases.answer: We establish exactly where you stand before touching anything. This is the paid audit, and it is the foundation for every claim made later.
steps: Kickoff call: your services, your three named competitors, your target area
Build 40-50 prompts from the questions patients actually ask
You sign off on the prompt set before any measurement happens
Run three passes per prompt across five engines under fixed conditions
Screenshot every result where a competitor appears and you do not
Technical, extractability and off-site audits
Prioritised roadmap, delivered on a walkthrough call
phases.outcome: A defensible baseline and a ranked fix list.

phases.name: Retrieval unblock
phases.answer: The fastest work in the engagement. Crawler access changes propagate within days, and the effect is visible in your own server logs almost immediately.
steps: Configure robots.txt for every major AI crawler
Publish llms.txt
Remove rendering blockers so content appears in raw HTML
Fix accidental noindex, broken canonicals and sitemap errors
Implement core structured data
Correct entity consistency across the web
Baseline and then monitor AI crawler hits in your logs
phases.outcome: Verifiable proof, in week one, that engines are now reaching you.

phases.name: On-site answer work
phases.answer: Restructuring content so an engine can lift a clean answer from it. Every section leads with a direct answer, headings mirror real questions, and claims stand on their own.
steps: Map prompts to pages and identify gaps
Rewrite key pages answer-first
Reshape headings into patient-question form
Build FAQ blocks with valid schema
Convert comparison content to semantic tables
Create definitional pages engines can quote directly
Attribute every statistic and surface last-updated dates
phases.outcome: Content an engine can extract without guessing.

phases.name: Off-site authority
phases.answer: Runs in parallel, not after. This is the slower half — earning the independent references and consistent presence that make an engine willing to name you.
steps: Claim and correct every directory and platform listing
Build review presence on the platforms engines actually read
Outreach for inclusion in the third-party lists engines cite
Publish an original data asset from your own practice
Editorial and digital PR placement
Knowledge base assessment where notability is genuinely met
phases.outcome: Trust signals that are hard to build and hard to displace.

phases.name: Monthly measurement
phases.answer: The same prompt set, the same conditions, every month. This is what turns the work into something you can actually judge.
steps: Re-run the full prompt set under identical conditions
Compute movement against baseline and against last cycle
Track competitor movement
Review crawler activity
Report per engine, never averaged
Set next cycle's priorities
phases.outcome: A trend line instead of an anecdote.

leadingIndicators.heading: What you will see before citations move
leadingIndicators.answer: Citations take four to twelve weeks, which is a long time to wait for a sign of life. So we report the things that move earlier and can be independently verified.

items.title: AI crawler activity in your logs
items.body: The clearest week-one evidence. GPTBot alone has been observed hitting sites thousands of times a day, so once access is unblocked the change shows up almost immediately. Before and after, from your own server.

items.title: Structured data validation
items.body: Before and after, against Google's own validator. Either it passes or it does not.

items.title: Prompt-set coverage
items.body: Being mentioned without being cited is still movement. We report it rather than waiting for the perfect number.

items.title: Snippets and People Also Ask
items.body: These respond faster than LLM citations. It is the speed advantage of the on-site half of the work.

items.title: Placements secured
items.body: A third-party reference is reportable the day it goes live, before any engine has cited it.
